sentences.text: Revenue rose from $41.9 billion in FY2016 to $47.9 billion in FY2025, a 1.5% CAGR [F1][F10][F219].
Revenue fell 11.4% in FY2020 [D195] and rose 17.1% in FY2021 [D246], so the window is a dip and recovery rather than steady compounding.
Operating income rose 37.7% in FY2025 to $13.8 billion [D450][F40], well above the 18.0% high before it [D94].
The filing attributes the FY2025 operating income increase mainly to lower other operating charges, which lapped the prior-year fairlife remeasurement [P12][D450].
Concentrate operations were the largest product contributor in FY2025, adding 1.6pp of the 1.9% revenue growth on a 59.4% revenue share [D534][D449][D532].
Within that, Non-US concentrate added 1.3pp [D548], while Non-US finished product operations subtracted 1.0pp [D555].
The filing cites 1% concentrate sales volume growth and favorable pricing as drivers of the FY2025 operating income gain [P12][D450].
Operating-cost growth ran 9.7pp below revenue growth in FY2025 [D474], the operating leverage behind the 7.5pp margin gain [D463].
Diluted EPS grew 23.6%, slightly ahead of net income's 23.3%, as the diluted share count fell 0.2% [D453][D451][D468].
The FY2025 operating margin of 28.7% [F50] is above the 26.0% window median [D766] and equals the window high [D765].
Other operating lines added 6.2pp to the FY2025 margin [D477], against 0.6pp from cost of revenue [D475] and 0.7pp from SG&A [D476].
Corporate's operating loss narrowed to $1.82 billion from $5.26 billion, which the filing attributes to lower other operating charges [P6].
Gross margin rose to 61.6% [F30] on favorable pricing and the prior-year refranchising, partly offset by currency and commodity costs [P14].
Other income fell to $1.07 billion in FY2025 [X100] from $1.99 billion in FY2024 [X99], when refranchising gains were booked [P3].
Operating cash flow of $7.41 billion [F100] was 0.57x net income of $13.1 billion [F60][D436], against 1.08x in FY2023 [D335].
Free cash flow margin was 11.0% [D433], below the 20.2% window median [D775]; capex was 4.4% of revenue [D432] and 2.01x D&A [D438].
The filing credits the FY2025 operating cash rise of 8.9% [D454] to lower tax payments and working-capital timing [P1].
The FY2024 operating cash drop of 41.3% [D404] followed the IRS Tax Litigation Deposit [P22].
Net cash was $8.78 billion at FY2025 [D442], or 18.3% of revenue [D443].
FY2024 total debt of $1.14 billion [D391] equals short-term borrowings alone [X185], against $41.7 billion in FY2023 [D340].
KO ranks at the 100th percentile for net cash against the staples peer group [D793], whose median is -14.5% [D794], but that rank rests on the incomplete debt line.
Dividends of $8.78 billion [X145] and buybacks of $746 million [X135] totaled $9.53 billion [D444], 179.9% of free cash flow [D445], while diluted shares fell only 0.2% [D468].
Buybacks and dividends ran at 105.1% of free cash flow in FY2023 [D344], 214.2% in FY2024 [D395] and 179.9% in FY2025 [D445].
Free cash flow was 0.45x and 0.40x net income in FY2024 and FY2025 [D387][D437], against a 0.97x window median [D778].
FY2017 and FY2018 revenue are recast: $36.2 billion and $34.3 billion [F2][F3] versus $35.4 billion and $31.9 billion first reported [X2][X3].
Total debt rose 31.3% in FY2025 [D470], but the FY2024 base is short-term borrowings alone [D391][X185], so the move is a data break, not new borrowing.
In the FY2026 10-K, operating margin staying above the 26.0% window median [D766] would confirm the FY2025 step-up, while a fall toward 21.2% [F49] would reverse it.
In the FY2026 10-K, free cash flow margin returning above the 20.2% window median [D775] would signal conversion recovery from 11.0% [D433].
In the FY2026 10-K, total debt should reconcile to FY2023's $41.7 billion [D340] plus later movements; if not, the FY2024 and FY2025 net cash figures [D392][D442] need restating.
